how_customers_find_and_choose: Buyers and traders are mostly reached through phone calls, chat groups and personal relationships built over years
Rates and availability are shared in chat groups, often with a photo or a short video of the produce or animal
Quality and trust are judged on sight, by reputation and by repeat dealing; direct-to-consumer sellers are starting to use chat and map listings
Farmers learn new methods from short videos and from neighbours who tried them first
what_works_now: Short phone-camera videos of the produce, animal, shed or field shown to buyers before they travel
A simple written record of each batch, animal or field: dates, feed or inputs, what was sold and to whom
A saved chat group or broadcast list of regular buyers told when a lot is ready
Direct sale of a graded, packed or branded portion to households, restaurants or shops for a better margin where the owner can handle the extra work
Writing down every delivery, weight and payment so disputes with traders end quickly
Weather and market rate checks before deciding when to sell, using trusted shared sources
Basic tidy packing and clean labelling for anything sold directly
outdated_or_weak: Advice to 'build a website' for a business whose buyers deal by phone and relationship
Generic 'go digital' or 'use social media' advice with no specific first step
Assuming the owner has steady internet, a computer or time to sit at one
Long forms or logins that the owner or workers will not use in the field
Copying urban retail marketing ideas such as flyers or loyalty cards

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Crop seasons, mandi days and weather decide the calendar; credit between traders and farmers is common
Eid al-Adha is the peak for sacrificial animals, with buyers booking weeks ahead
Connectivity in rural areas can be weak; voice notes and short videos work better than long typed messages
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Farms and stables often serve a niche market of private buyers, restaurants and tourists
Animal and food businesses are subject to municipal and veterinary rules; the owner checks them with the authority
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Direct-to-consumer and farm-gate sales, farmers markets and subscription boxes exist alongside large buyers
Farming has strict animal welfare and food rules by province; the owner checks them with the relevant authority

never_assume: A smartphone with steady data, or any computer
A website, a social page or a customer list
Written records of the farm beyond a notebook
Cold storage or transport of their own
